topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Average Rate of Change
lecture_lines: Average speed is distance divided by time.
Visualize the slope of a secant line.
animations: Show title 'Average Rate of Change' in #FFFFFF.
Display average speed formula v = d/t in #FFFF00.
Draw Cartesian axes #FFFFFF with secant line connecting two points on a curve in #FF00FF.

sections.title: The Problem of 'Instantaneous'
lecture_lines: How fast at exactly two seconds?
Zoom in until points nearly coincide.
Secant line approaches the tangent line.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative via Limits
lecture_lines: Derivative is limit as interval shrinks.
Formally, f prime of x limit notation.
Slope represents instantaneous rate of change.
Ball path shows changing tangent slope.
Slope is positive, zero, then negative.
animations: Draw box around final 'f'(x)' result in #00FF00. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ball.svg]

sections.title: Graphical Interpretation and Application
lecture_lines: Derivative equals slope of tangent line.
It measures instantaneous rate of change.
Think of your car's speedometer reading.
Instantaneous speed means speed right now.
animations: Display curve f(x)=x^2 and tangent line at x=1 in #FFFFFF.
Draw line indicating f'(1)=2 slope in #FF00FF.
Animate speedometer needle [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg] moving based on derivative value.
